parsed.explanation: The combined regime imposes universal-exposure exposures at the national layer: passport sex fixed at assigned birth, X markers ended, entry officers instructed to refuse cases with document/sex discrepancies and to weigh fraud findings, and detention/custody harms documented (corrections conversion-style policies, immigration-custody forced labour and sexual abuse). The division adds a fixed-at-birth executive order, birth-sex custody with a documented assault dismissed by courts, an under-19 care ban (directly binding a trans minor visitor and a travelling guardian), and no state gender-identity hate-crime or anti-discrimination statute. Mitigations: no local criminal facility statute documented, no sodomy law, national hate-crime coverage, marriage/adoption recognition, municipal protections, functioning courts and ongoing litigation. Severity centres on exclusion, humiliation, detention and care denial rather than imprisonment or death, but the exposure is continuous at borders and in custody. This matches the 0.45 tier: universal document/records friction with inconsistent enforcement, partial recourse, no lethal pathway.

entry_documents.exposure: Passports must show sex assigned at birth; X markers ended; entry officers refuse cases on discrepancy and may weigh lifetime fraud ineligibility; passports confiscated or blocked with travellers stranded; allied governments issued advisories.
entry_documents.protection: Fraud finding requires four elements, never automatic; existing X passports valid until expiry; litigation ongoing.
entry_documents.interaction: Document mismatch at entry can trigger refusal, secondary investigation, or downstream custody exposure.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: National corrections policies mandate conversion-style treatment of trans inmates, hormone removal, stopped reporting; immigration custody shows forced labour, beatings, solitary, sexual abuse. Division practice houses trans women by birth sex; documented assault by celled sex offender dismissed by courts.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: National hate-crime statute covers gender identity; courts function.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: Any arrest or immigration matter can lead to birth-sex custody.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: National order bars congruent facility use in government-funded single-sex facilities; facility bans in many state/provinces, criminal offences in 4; division executive order backs single-sex bathrooms/changing rooms; a trans woman's capitol-restroom arrest documented in another division.
federal_state_facilities.protection: In this division no enforcement statute is documented; trespass trigger requires refusal to depart, and is not shown adopted locally.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: Facility use exposes visitor to confrontation, ejection, or police call depending on state.

care_services.exposure: Division bans gender-affirming care under 19; a visitor under 19 cannot obtain care and a guardian cannot obtain it for a minor; national rules proposed barring public-insurance reimbursement for trans minors; hospitals subpoenaed for minors' records.
care_services.protection: Adult visitors' routine care not documented as restricted here; national employment/housing recognition partly operative.
care_services.interaction: A travelling family faces care denial and potential records scrutiny.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: Federal framing of 'radical gender ideology' in counterterrorism guidance; order directing prosecution of teachers facilitating minor transitions; state order erases recognition of trans people; 2026 legislative degradation continuing.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: Several orders enjoined in court; counterterrorism guidance disclaims targeting mere disagreement.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: Framing raises discovery probability and legitimises official hostility across levels.

minors_guardians.exposure: Under-19 care ban upheld by division supreme court; guardian cannot secure care for a trans minor; school-activity rules and sports ban; federal prosecution threats against facilitators; records subpoenas for minors.
minors_guardians.interaction: Travelling with a trans minor converts care access and school/facility rules into direct exposure.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: No division trans-violence statistics documented; no state gender-identity hate-crime coverage; documented restroom arrest elsewhere shows police enforcement pattern.
street_violence_police_response.protection: National hate-crime statute covers gender identity; division hate-crime law enforced for perceived-association bias; municipal protections in one city.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Bias offence chargeable nationally where state law silent.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: Post-2023 division marker rules beyond surgery requirements unresolved; several federal measures in litigation, operative status varies by travel date; division custody recourse failed (dismissal with de minimis findings).
remedies_unknowns.protection: Legal-aid FAQ and ongoing suits; national housing/employment enforcement operates; marriage and adoption recognition settled.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Remedies partial and uneven; unremedied recurring practices treated as exposure, not mitigation.

anchor_checks.comparison: Less severe: unlike Vellandra's routine entry refusal apparatus, entry refusals here are documented but not near-universal, and most visitors clear screening; lifetime fraud findings are discretionary. But the document regime is similarly universal in design, keeping this jurisdiction well below 0.55.

Materially worse than Kestrel Isles: secondary screening there yields administrative denial with working appeal desks, while here the worst documented features are tier-1 (documents that cannot be made to match, birth-sex custody with assault, hormone removal in custody) and official threat-framing, so the case sits below that anchor.

Well below Meridia: there trained border officers and a functioning tribunal release detainees with remedies; here custody practice is documented as harmful and unremedied, care for minors is banned, and state policy denies recognition — litigation is contested, not protective.

Closely matched: routine document/record exposure, detention unlikely except as fraud allegations, outcomes varying by locale, no custodial sentence typical, no execution — consistent with this jurisdiction's combined regime.

parsed.synthesis: The operative regime combines a national document system that forces assigned-sex markers, entry officers primed to refuse discrepant cases and weigh fraud findings, and federal custody practices documented as abusive, with a division layer that denies trans recognition, houses prisoners by birth sex with documented assault and judicial dismissal, bans under-19 care, and offers no state gender-identity hate-crime or anti-discrimination statute. These are universal-exposure, tier-1 features: every trans visitor crosses a border desk and carries documents that cannot be conformed, and an arrest route leads into birth-sex custody. Partial mitigations — national hate-crime coverage, marriage/adoption recognition, municipal protections, functioning courts, and ongoing litigation — reduce severity but, per the record, have not remedied the recurring practices. No lethal pathway is documented, but exclusion, detention, humiliation and care denial are. Result: solidly Elevated Risk, comparable to the 0.45 anchors.
